Inside Sales Manager

Sales & Customer Support

Køge, Denmark

Your impact begins here

Take ownership of our important transactional customer segment and make it easier for customers to do business with us. As our Inside Sales Manager, you will combine commercial judgement with responsive customer service, helping customers move efficiently from inquiry and quotation to purchasing decision. As this is a newly created role, you will have the opportunity to shape how we work with this customer segment and establish effective ways of working from the start.

What you'll bring

B2b sales experience from a regulated or highly documented industry, such as pharmaceuticals, biopharmaceuticals, medical devices, chemicals or food. You enjoy customer contact and know how to combine excellent service with commercial focus. You are structured, proactive and comfortable managing multiple opportunities without losing momentum or attention to detail.

We are looking for:

• Experience in inside sales, sales support, account coordination, customer service, business development or another customer-facing commercial role.

• Strong communication skills and confidence engaging customers by phone, email and virtual meetings.

• Experience preparing quotations or commercial proposals and following opportunities through to completion.

• A commercial mindset and confidence discussing pricing and commercial terms.

• Strong organisational skills and a disciplined approach to commercial follow-up.

• Experience using Salesforce or a similar CRM system.

What you'll do

• Own the commercial relationship with a portfolio of smaller and transactional customers.

• Handle customer inquiries, quotations and commercial transactions, helping customers move efficiently through the purchasing process.

• Understand and qualify customer needs and provide clear information about products, services, pricing and commercial terms.

• Organise and prioritise leads and opportunities, maintaining consistent follow-up and commercial momentum.

• Keep customer, opportunity and pipeline information accurate and up to date in Salesforce.

• Collaborate with sales, customer support and technical experts, ensuring smooth handovers when additional expertise is needed.

Who you'll work with

You will join the Sales & Customer Support team within Novo Nordisk Pharmatech's Sales & Marketing organisation. The wider area consists of approximately 35 colleagues across Sales & Customer Support, Launch Office, Strategic Marketing, New Product Marketing and Commercial Excellence, with most colleagues based in Køge.

You will work closely with sales colleagues, customer support and technical experts to find the right solutions for customers and keep opportunities moving forward.

Novo Nordisk Pharmatech is a wholly owned subsidiary of Novo Nordisk with approximately 450 employees across Research and Development, Business Development, Manufacturing, Marketing and Sales. With more than 75 years of experience, we support life-science innovation through specialised knowledge, collaboration and scientific expertise.

What you can expect here

This role gives you ownership of an important customer segment and the opportunity to help establish a new commercial function. You will have significant customer interaction and the freedom to improve processes and develop effective ways of working.

You will work in an international environment serving customers in the pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical industries, where commercial responsiveness goes hand in hand with consistent quality.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 651,000 to 956,900 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate's skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may be eligible to earn performance-based incentive compensation, short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks. Learn more about our Reward Philosophy.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to make it easier for customers to do business with us while turning commercial opportunities into results, apply for the Inside Sales Manager role by 6 December

Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

For questions, please reach out to Anders Møller Koefoed, omoe@novonordisk.com.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

Your impact begins here

As Senior IT Infrastructure Project Manager, you will lead global projects that standardise, strengthen and expand the IT Infrastructure Novo relies on every day, from existing buildings to expansion projects. You will turn business needs into practical plans and deliver them with minimal disruption to production. Your work makes our infrastructure more resilient, secure and efficient, so colleagues across Novo can keep making progress for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

• A B.Sc. or higher in IT, engineering, project management or an analytical field, or equivalent practical experience.

• 8+ years of experience delivering IT infrastructure projects in large organisations. Demonstrated results matter more to us than formal certifications.

• Strong planning, stakeholder and vendor management skills, and the ability to take ownership across functions.

• Comfort working in a global environment with many internal and external stakeholders.

• Fluent English, excellent communication skills, independence and the ability to collaborate across cultures.

What you’ll do

You will own the delivery of infrastructure projects that shape how Novo’s IT estate runs, across both greenfield and brownfield environments and across production and non-production.

• Lead projects from scope to closure across global sites, including planning, budget, timeline, risk and execution.

• Translate business needs into clear technical requirements and practical implementation plans.

• Coordinate multidisciplinary teams, including network and security engineers, operations, vendors and local site IT.

• Oversee projects in areas such as network, network security, virtualisation and backup, and drive modernisation through automation and standardisation of global setups.

• Assess impact and risk to minimise disruption to production, and support urgent site-level priorities when they arise.

• Help the team strengthen project governance, change control, status reporting and stakeholder communication

• Mentor and empower team members colleagues in an inclusive, collaborative culture.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Infrastructure Projects within Infrastructure & Information Security, part of Enterprise IT & Quality. We are a team of 10+ project managers and solution architects based in Denmark and the US, planning, designing and delivering infrastructure projects across Novo worldwide.

Day to day, you will work with network and security engineers, operations teams, vendors and local site IT, as well as business stakeholders across countries and cultures. We use an internal project model and governance framework for large-scale projects, which gives us consistent oversight, clear decision-making and successful global delivery. Where it helps, we work in iterations with cross-functional teams.

What you can expect here

You will work in a team that values curiosity, continuous learning and knowledge sharing. We care about psychological safety and a supportive environment where everyone’s contribution matters, and you will be trusted to take ownership and make your voice heard. Working across countries, cultures and functions will broaden your perspective and help you build new skills through hands-on delivery.

Salary

For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 742,600.00 to 1,091,600.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to lead the infrastructure projects that keep Novo’s global IT estate resilient, secure and ready for what comes next, apply for the Senior IT Infrastructure Project Manager role by 7 December 2026.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

Specialty Care, Medical & Translational Science

Søborg, Denmark

Your impact begins here

As Director of one of our cardiovascular teams, you will lead eight medical specialists who provide medical and scientific expertise across our cardiovascular programmes. You will ensure high-quality and timely delivery while developing the people and capabilities needed as the portfolio grows. By combining scientific insight with inclusive leadership, you will help advance early- and late-stage clinical development in an area of strategic importance.

What you’ll bring

You are an experienced clinical drug development professional who enjoys leading highly skilled specialists. As a leader, you create clarity and direction while giving people the trust and space to take ownership. You are curious about different perspectives, communicate openly and build strong relationships across disciplines. At the same time, you stay close enough to the science to ask the right questions, provide guidance and support sound decisions when the evidence is complex or incomplete.

You balance people leadership with scientific and business priorities. Through clear expectations and constructive feedback, you create an environment where specialists can grow, contribute their expertise and work effectively together. You are comfortable navigating different perspectives and building alignment across functions and organisational levels.

For this role, we are looking for:

• A medical degree.

• Substantial experience in clinical drug development, including the development of clinical strategies and plans, clinical trial design and oversight, and interpretation of clinical data.

• Experience in line management, including coaching and developing specialists.

• Experience working cross-functionally and communicating medical and scientific recommendations to project teams and senior stakeholders.

• A PhD or equivalent research experience would be an advantage.

What you’ll do

• Lead, coach and develop a team of eight medical specialists, supporting their professional growth and enabling them to take increasing ownership of their work.

• Set clear priorities and allocate the team’s capacity across programmes to support high-quality and timely delivery.

• Oversee the team’s medical and scientific contributions to clinical development plans, trial protocols, study conduct and clinical documents.

• Identify scientific or operational issues that could affect delivery and work with programme leads and cross-functional partners to agree practical solutions.

• Prepare the team for internal governance discussions and communicate critical medical and scientific considerations to senior stakeholders.

• Work with the Senior Director and fellow Directors to shape the area’s direction, strengthen collaboration and develop the capabilities required for a growing portfolio.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Specialty Care, Cardiovascular & Liver Disease within Medical & Translational Science and report directly to the Senior Director. As part of the area leadership team, you will work closely with fellow Directors to coordinate priorities, share expertise and develop the organisation’s scientific and leadership capabilities.

Your key partners will include global project and clinical development teams, as well as colleagues across Research, Clinical Operations, Biostatistics, Safety, Regulatory Affairs and Global Medical Affairs. You will also engage with investigators, steering committees and external advisers to support clinical trial conduct and place clinical results in the appropriate scientific and medical context.

What you can expect here

You will take responsibility for an established team and have genuine scope to shape how the team works, collaborates and develops. The combination of early- and late-stage programmes will give you the opportunity to address a broad range of scientific and clinical development questions.

You will work in an international environment where your medical and leadership expertise can influence important decisions. You will be supported by the area leadership team as you build relationships, establish priorities and continue to develop in the role.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 940,800.00 to 1,448,700.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks. Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to lead and develop medical specialists whose expertise will help advance our cardiovascular portfolio, apply for the position as Cardiovascular team Director (people manager) by 6 December 2026.

Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. For questions, please reach out to Anton Wulf Christensen, awuc@novonordisk.com.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

Your impact begins here

As Clinical Pharmacology Specialist, you will bring scientific expertise to the development of innovative medicines across our growing global portfolio. From early clinical development through to regulatory new drug applications and health authority interactions, you will influence critical decisions on study design, dose selection and data interpretation. Your work helps turn science into therapies that improve the lives of patients and moves programmes forward with scientific excellence.

What you’ll bring

You bring a strong scientific foundation, combined with a collaborative and solution-oriented mindset.

• A Master’s degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Medicine, Pharmacology or a related discipline, combined with a PhD or equivalent scientific expertise.

• Experience within clinical pharmacology, gained in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, CRO or academic sector.

• Understanding of clinical drug development, including exposure to dose-setting strategies, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and translational science.

• Experience planning, conducting and interpreting clinical studies, while working effectively in cross-functional and international environments.

• Strong stakeholder management, communication and influencing skills.

• Proficiency in written and spoken English.

• A proactive, highly collaborative approach, motivated by scientific problem-solving. You take ownership of your responsibilities, challenge established thinking constructively and keep a strong focus on quality and delivery.

• Comfort operating in a dynamic environment, alongside talented colleagues who share your drive to advance science and improve patient outcomes.

What you’ll do

You will bring scientific expertise within Clinical Pharmacology, driving activities across development programmes and ensuring scientific excellence in study design, data interpretation and strategic decision-making. Day to day, you will:

• Lead the scientific planning, design, execution, interpretation and communication of clinical pharmacology studies across early and late-stage development programmes.

• Provide strategic clinical pharmacology input to development projects, including dose selection, PK/PD evaluations and benefit-risk assessments.

• Drive and coordinate clinical pharmacology activities across cross-functional project teams and external collaborations throughout the value chain.

• Contribute to regulatory documentation, health authority interactions and submission activities that support the approval of new medicines globally.

• Represent Clinical Pharmacology in development teams, collaborating with internal experts, external partners and scientific leaders to advance programmes efficiently.

Success in this position takes strong scientific curiosity, the ability to navigate complex development challenges, and confidence in communicating evidence-based recommendations to diverse stakeholders.

Who you’ll work with

In Research & Development, colleagues explore scientific ideas and advance them towards clinical testing. You will join the Clinical Pharmacology organisation, made up of five Clinical Pharmacology departments and an integrated part of Medical and Translational Sciences.

Clinical Pharmacology works as part of development and research project teams. The organisation is responsible for the clinical pharmacology strategy and the scientific input to clinical pharmacology trials, and provides expertise to all clinical development phases, Health Authority interactions and regulatory submissions worldwide.

Your closest partners will be development project teams and headquarters-based study groups. You will also work with affiliates, external partners across the value chain, key opinion leaders and Health Authorities – bringing perspectives together so decisions are clear and projects keep their momentum.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take ownership and make your voice heard, in a team that values scientific curiosity and constructive challenge. We offer continuous learning and career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage, so you can grow, contribute and perform at your best.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 742,600.00 to 1,091,600.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area, and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to shape the development of innovative medicines as Clinical Pharmacology Specialist, apply by 6 December 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

Are you passionate about making knowledge accessible, reliable, and useful? Join Novo to shape how we manage and share knowledge across global Customer Service, helping our teams deliver consistent, efficient, and valuable support to customers.

Your new role

As Knowledge Manager, you will own and drive the global knowledge management approach within Customer Service Excellence. You will establish the governance, processes, and ways of working that ensure relevant knowledge is captured, maintained, shared, and used effectively across markets and service providers.

Working closely with affiliates and global stakeholders, you will balance global consistency with local needs and embed knowledge management into everyday Customer Service operations. This includes developing a trusted knowledge base, strengthening knowledge-sharing behaviors, and enabling self-service and AI-supported Customer Service. You will apply relevant methods, including Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS), where they add value.

Your main responsibilities will include:

• Own and develop global knowledge management: Define the approach, standards, roles, and responsibilities for managing Customer Service knowledge across markets and channels.

• Establish governance and ensure quality: Set clear expectations for knowledge ownership, creation, approval, review, and retirement, ensuring alignment with relevant quality requirements and SOPs.

• Strengthen knowledge availability and reuse: Bring together fragmented knowledge, improve its structure and accessibility, and balance globally shared content with local requirements.

• Drive implementation and adoption: Embed practical knowledge management processes into daily workflows, drawing on KCS principles to support knowledge capture, reuse, and improvement through customer interactions.

• Collaborate with affiliates and service providers: Align ways of working, support onboarding and service transitions, and follow up on knowledge quality, contributions, and adoption.

• Measure value and improve continuously: Monitor knowledge quality, usage, and service outcomes. Use feedback and customer enquiry trends to identify gaps and improve content and processes.

• Enable digital Customer Service: Partner with self-service, AI, and technology colleagues to ensure knowledge is suitable for use across service channels and solutions.

• This is an individual contributor role with global reach, where you will create impact through expertise, collaboration, and influence across functions, markets, and external partners.

Your new department

You will join the Customer Service Excellence team, working to strengthen the global Customer Service experience through consistent processes, effective governance, and continuous improvement.

Working closely with affiliates, Customer Service partners, and colleagues across quality, safety, commercial, and digital functions, you will translate operational needs into practical, scalable ways of working. Your contribution will help ensure that reliable knowledge supports both our Customer Service teams and the continued development of self-service and AI-supported service.

Your skills & qualifications

We are looking for someone who combines practical knowledge management experience with the ability to establish clear processes and help people adopt new ways of working.

To succeed in this role, you bring:

• A bachelor’s or master’s degree in business, knowledge management, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

• Three to five years or more of hands-on knowledge management experience.

• Experience developing knowledge governance, content standards, and processes for creating, maintaining, and sharing knowledge.

• A strong understanding of Customer Service operations and how effective knowledge management improves service quality and efficiency.

• Experience working with external service providers, including setting expectations and following up on performance.

• Strong facilitation, training, and stakeholder management skills, with experience driving adoption across teams.

• An analytical, quality-focused mindset and the ability to translate feedback and data into practical improvements.

• Experience with KCS or similar approaches is an advantage, as is experience from pharma or another regulated industry. You communicate clearly, work independently, and build strong relationships across cultures and time zones. You are comfortable influencing without formal authority and motivated by making knowledge useful for others.

Working at Novo Nordisk

Every day we seek the solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. To do this, we approach our work with determination, constant curiosity and a commitment to finding better ways forward. For over 100 years, this dedication has driven us to build a company focused on lasting change for long-term health. One where diverse thinking, shared purpose and mutual respect come together to create extraordinary results. When you join us, you're not just starting a job – you're becoming part of a story that spans generations.

What we offer

At Novo Nordisk, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Salary:  For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 651,000.00 to 956,900.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level,  location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Deadline

6th December 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

Your impact begins here

Consumer engagement in healthcare is changing quickly, creating new opportunities as well as new legal questions. As Associate General Counsel, Consumer Partnerships, you will help shape how Novo Nordisk engages directly with consumers and builds external partnerships responsibly.

You will work alongside the business as new capabilities, partnerships and operating models take shape, helping turn ambitious ideas into practical solutions while navigating an evolving legal and regulatory environment.

What you'll bring

You are an experienced lawyer who combines sound legal judgement with a practical understanding of business. You are comfortable working in areas where the business model and legal framework may still be developing.

We are looking for:

• A law degree or equivalent legal qualification, such as an LL.M. or J.D.

• Substantial relevant legal experience, preferably including experience working in-house.

• Experience advising businesses in complex or highly regulated environments.

• Relevant experience in areas such as strategic partnerships, consumer-facing services, technology or regulated healthcare.

• Strong commercial judgement and the ability to translate complex legal considerations into clear, actionable advice.

• Experience collaborating with and influencing senior stakeholders across functions and geographies.

Experience from pharmaceutical or healthcare organisations would be an advantage. We are also interested in relevant experience from consumer, technology, media, platform, government, consumer health or other highly regulated industries.

What you'll do

Your focus will be on enabling responsible consumer engagement and partnerships while helping the business navigate new and evolving legal questions. You will:

• Provide proactive and strategic legal advice to senior leaders and teams developing consumer partnerships and engagement capabilities.

• Help shape new consumer engagement models and identify legally viable ways forward where established approaches may not yet exist.

• Advise on consumer-facing initiatives across digital channels, social media, platforms, partnerships and emerging forms of engagement.

• Structure, draft and negotiate strategic partnerships and commercial arrangements with external organisations.

• Navigate legal and regulatory considerations across areas including pharmaceutical and consumer marketing, digital platforms, privacy and data use, and competition law.

• Translate complex requirements into practical frameworks and approaches that enable progress while appropriately managing legal risk.

Who you'll work with

You will join Product & Portfolio Strategy Legal, part of Novo Nordisk's global Legal, Ethics & Compliance organisation. The team provides strategic legal support across important commercial, medical and corporate activities, working closely with senior business leaders and colleagues across functions and geographies. You will be a principal legal partner to parts of the newly established Consumer Care organisation, with a particular focus on Consumer Partnerships. You will also collaborate with Legal, Ethics & Compliance colleagues and teams across headquarters, International Operations, regions and affiliates. As these consumer capabilities continue to develop, you will have a genuine opportunity to influence both individual initiatives and the broader legal frameworks and ways of working that support them globally.

What you can expect here

This is an opportunity to work where healthcare, consumer engagement, digital innovation and strategic partnerships meet. You will have room to apply your expertise while helping develop legal approaches for areas that do not always come with established answers. Your work will have both immediate business relevance and the potential to shape how Novo Nordisk approaches consumer engagement more broadly.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 847,000.00 to 1,245,100.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks. Learn more about our Reward Philosophy.

Start now

Your impact begins today.

If you are ready to help shape responsible consumer engagement and partnerships in an evolving healthcare environment, apply for the Associate General Counsel, Consumer Partnerships role by 3rd December 2026.

VP of Infrastructure, Enterprise IT

Technology infrastructure is the foundation that enables innovation, research, manufacturing and commercial excellence at scale. As VP of Infrastructure, you will shape and lead Novo’s global infrastructure strategy, ensuring a resilient, secure and future-ready technology landscape that supports millions of patients worldwide.

Your new role

As VP of Infrastructure, you will lead the strategy, operations and continuous evolution of Novo’s global technology infrastructure and workplace services landscape. You will play a critical role in ensuring our global technology foundation remains resilient, scalable and secure while supporting ambitious growth and digital transformation initiatives across the organisation. You will report to the Senior Vice President of Enterprise Platforms, and head up and organization of app. 250 employees.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Defining and driving the global infrastructure strategy, aligning technology investments with business priorities, digital transformation ambitions and long-term growth objectives.

• Leading the delivery and optimisation of core infrastructure services, including cloud platforms, networks, servers, storage, identity solutions and workplace technologies.

• Ensuring operational excellence through robust service management, disaster recovery capabilities, business continuity preparedness and supplier governance.

• Partnering closely with cybersecurity, compliance and business leaders to strengthen resilience, manage risks and enable secure-by-design technology platforms.

• Building and leading a high-performing global organisation while fostering innovation within cloud technologies, automation, observability, platform engineering and modern workplace solutions.

Your new department

Enterprise IT & Quality (EITQ) plays a key role in enabling Novo to operate, grow and innovate at global scale. The area brings together enterprise technology, digital capabilities and quality expertise to deliver secure, reliable and compliant solutions across the organisation. Working closely with colleagues across the business, EITQ helps strengthen our technology foundation, advance digital transformation and ensure that quality remains embedded in the way we work.

Your skills and qualifications

We are looking for an inspirational infrastructure leader who thrives in complex global environments and can combine strategic thinking with operational excellence. You are comfortable navigating across business and technology domains and have a proven ability to influence at executive level.

To succeed in this role, you will bring:

• Extensive senior leadership experience within IT infrastructure, technology operations or digital platform leadership in large global organisations.

• Deep expertise across cloud platforms, enterprise infrastructure, networking, service management, disaster recovery and modern workplace technologies.

• A strong track record of leading large-scale transformations, building high-performing teams and developing organisational capability.

• Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with experience engaging executives and senior business leaders across complex organisations.

• A strategic, future-oriented mindset combined with sound decision-making, operational risk awareness and the ability to lead through change and ambiguity.

Experience with large-scale cloud transformation programmes, identity platforms and global supplier ecosystems will be considered an advantage.

Deadline

Decmber 13.

For further information about the position, please contact Executive Search Advisor Kristoffer Baadsgaard on +45 3077 5605.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

Lead Data Engineer

Category:  Data & AI

Location:

Ballerup, Capital Region of Denmark, DK

Your impact begins here

As Lead Data Engineer in Commercial AI & Data, you will build the data foundation that business teams, data scientists and AI product teams rely on every day. You will decide independently which approaches and techniques best prepare and deliver data, and turn business needs into scalable, trusted data assets. Your work helps AI and analytics reach the people who use them, supporting Novo's work for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

• 
Master’s degree in Computer Science, Statistics, Engineering or a related field.

• 
8+ years of experience in data engineering, data architecture or data product development, with a focus on designing and delivering large-scale data initiatives.

• 
In-depth knowledge of cloud and data platforms, including Azure, Databricks, AWS and Snowflake.

• 
Hands-on programming experience in Python, SQL and Spark.

• 
Deep expertise in ETL/ELT design, data modelling, data warehousing and data lakes, and streaming technologies such as Kafka and Event Hubs.

• 
A strong DataOps and DevOps background, including Git, CI/CD pipelines, Docker and Kubernetes.

• 
Experience with first-party consumer and patient data in a pharmaceutical company.

• 
Solid understanding of master data management, data quality, lineage, cataloguing and policy management tools and practices.

• 
Practical experience with the architecture, implementation, DevOps and support of data platforms.

• 
Experience working in cross-functional, matrix teams, and the ability to communicate with colleagues at all levels.

• 
Highly proficient English, written and spoken.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience in the pharmaceutical industry or another regulated environment.

What you’ll do

You will lead how Novo’s commercial data is designed, built and used, from the first architecture decision to a reliable product in production.

• 
Design enterprise-scale data architectures and pipelines, defining data models, storage strategies, integration patterns and standards for how data is ingested, transformed and consumed.

• 
Lead the development of robust ETL/ELT pipelines for batch and real-time processing, keeping data quality, reliability and performance high and resolving complex engineering issues.

• 
Build the data foundations for AI, machine learning and advanced analytics, including feature stores, data products and self-service analytics capabilities.

• 
Implement data governance, security and privacy standards, including metadata management, lineage, cataloguing, master data and data quality initiatives.

• 
Provide technical direction to data engineers through architecture and code reviews, mentoring, and shared engineering best practices and design patterns.

• 
Lead large-scale data engineering projects across multiple teams, managing technical risks and dependencies, optimising performance and cost, and putting monitoring and alerting in place so work lands with quality, within scope and on schedule.

Who you’ll work with

You will be part of Commercial AI & Data within Enterprise IT & Quality. Colleagues here work across the Novo value chain, stay close to the business and help deliver trusted technology, high quality and responsible ways of working. The focus is on ensuring the highest quality for patients, being a trusted tech leader and being an environmentally responsible business.

You will provide technical direction to data engineers and work side by side with business stakeholders, data scientists, analysts and AI product teams. You will translate business requirements into scalable technical solutions, explain technical concepts in plain language to non-technical colleagues, and influence platform roadmaps and priorities. Close collaboration, clear decisions and the pace to follow them through are how this work moves forward.

What you can expect here

You will take ownership of technical decisions that shape how data is built and used, and your expertise will be trusted and heard. You will set engineering standards, mentor colleagues and influence platform roadmaps, growing your own skills as you help others grow theirs.

You will join the forefront of AI and technology, as Novo upskills its entire workforce to advance AI for people living with serious chronic diseases. Expectations are clear, results are recognised, and you will be supported to thrive and perform at your best.

Salary

For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 742,600.00 to 1,091,600.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to build the data foundation behind Novo’s commercial AI and analytics, apply for the Lead Data Engineer role by 2 December 2026. Lasting health starts now, and so can your contribution.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.occupation: Regulatory Principal Specialist, Global Regulatory Lead
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

We are looking for Regulatory Principal Specialists to take on the role of Global Regulatory Lead for projects within the Cardiovascular and Cardiometabolic Health therapeutic areas. We are looking for global regulatory leads that can operate in the early development space as well in Phase 2 and towards submission. As such you will lead the development of the regulatory strategy for development programmes with several molecules and multiple indications and help design development programmes that enables the strategy. Your strategic input will shape project direction and decisions, and your work will make an impact across Novo Nordisk's early portfolio.

What you'll bring

You combine a strong scientific background with extensive regulatory drug development experience and an understanding of the pharmaceutical value chain. To succeed in this role, you should have:

• 
An academic degree, such as a master's degree and/or a PhD, within life science, health science or a related field.

• 
Extensive regulatory experience on global drug development programmes (minimum 8–10 years).

• 
A proven track record of interacting directly with international regulatory authorities, such as the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the European Medicines Agency (EMA).

• 
Experience working across several Regulatory Affairs domains, such as clinical, chemistry, manufacturing and controls (CMC), headquarters, affiliate and/or regional office.

• 
Experience leading teams through informal or formal leadership roles.

• 
Fluency in written and spoken English.

Useful, but not essential: advanced regulatory knowledge across several therapeutic areas, preferably within obesity, diabetes and/or cardiovascular.

On a personal level, you bring strong negotiation and stakeholder management skills, and you can adjust your communication style to suit different audiences. You drive innovation, look for ways to optimise processes, and thrive in collaborative teams. A positive, can-do attitude and the composure to keep a sense of humour in high-pressure situations will help you succeed.

What you'll do

• 
Lead the development of the regulatory strategy for a cardiovascular or cardiometabolic programme, potentially with several molecules and multiple indications, ensuring that the regulatory path is clear.

• 
Help design ambitious development programmes that enable the regulatory strategy.

• 
Represent Global Regulatory Affairs in the global project team and other cross-functional teams, providing strategic input to the development plan and assessing regulatory opportunities, risks and mitigation strategies.

• 
Plan, prepare and lead interactions with health authorities around the world.

• 
Be accountable for regulatory documents, such as briefing packages for health authority interactions, paediatric plans, clinical trial applications and labelling documents.

• 
Mentor more junior colleagues and share your expertise to support their professional development.

Who you'll work with

Do you want to contribute to environmental and planning work on Energinet’s infrastructure projects? Can you help deliver environmental assessments, planning processes and/or applications for permits and exemptions? Whether you are early in your career or bring extensive relevant experience, explore the consultant opportunities below and join our team in COWI.

Create the solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

To help handle environmental issues, we are looking for a Senior Consultant to join COWI and support our client Energinet, on construction and reinvestment projects in the Danish electricity infrastructure. Following an introduction to Energinet’s processes, methods and systems, you will work independently on one or more projects, primarily involving onshore infrastructure. The role entails environmental screening and assessment of onshore facilities, planning documentation, applications for exemptions and permits under planning and environmental legislation, and sub-project management. Depending on your experience, you will contribute as a senior consultant or as a consultant/junior consultant.

Your key responsibilities will depend on the assignment and your level of expertise.

For senior consultants, tasks may include, but are not limited to:

• Preparing environmental screenings and environmental assessments.

• Preparing environmental impact assessments.

• Supporting the preparation of planning documentation under the Danish Planning Act.

• Planning and coordinating preliminary investigations for environmental assessments.

• Managing projects or sub-projects, including the control, leadership and administration of project activities, schedules, resource use, project finances and the quality of deliverables.

• Coordinating and carrying out environmental assessment and planning processes with internal and external stakeholders, including authorities.

• Preparing presentations, discussion papers and brief analyses of specific issues to support coordination with authorities and members of the public, among other purposes.

• Working as part of a team of sub-project managers, planning and environmental specialists and other project staff to deliver project-related work on assigned projects.

For consultants and junior consultants, tasks may include, but are not limited to:

• Working as part of a team of sub-project managers, environmental specialists and other project staff to deliver project-related work on assigned projects.

• Preparing applications for exemptions and permits under nature and environmental sector legislation before construction work begins.

• Preparing environmental screenings for linear infrastructure projects.

• Coordinating with internal and external stakeholders, including authorities and landowners.

• Undertaking ad hoc project tasks relating to environmental matters.

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

The first step to success in this role is that you are eager to collaborate with the people around you, whether they are colleagues, partners or customers. Developing ties with others is something you do by acting respectfully and delivering on your promises. And you never get set in your ways, but keep exploring new insights and ways to improve.

Your technical skills and experience will depend on your experience.

For senior consultants, relevant competencies include:

• Familiarity with the Danish Environmental Assessment Act and Planning Act, as well as applicable nature and environmental legislation generally.

• Several years of experience assessing impacts on environmental parameters and the ability to manage environmental assessment processes.

• Several years of experience preparing environmental screenings (VVM screenings) and environmental impact assessments (formerly VVM reports).

• Several years of experience preparing planning documents under the Danish Planning Act.

• An understanding of authority approval processes for linear infrastructure projects, including stakeholder involvement.

• Skills and experience in solution-oriented teamwork and project work, with the ability to maintain an overview of complex processes.

• Experience communicating with authorities, landowners and members of the public.

• Experience from similar infrastructure projects.

• Strong communication skills in both Danish and English.

For consultants and junior consultants working with exemptions and permits, relevant competencies include:

• Familiarity with applicable nature and environmental legislation generally.

• Experience preparing applications for exemptions and permits under environmental and nature sector legislation.

• Some experience with ecological site surveys and assessments concerning Annex IV species.

• Some experience communicating with authorities and landowners.

• Some experience preparing environmental screenings (VVM screenings).

• An understanding of authority approval processes for linear infrastructure projects, including stakeholder involvement.

• A few years of experience from similar infrastructure projects.

• Strong communication skills in both Danish and English.

Working arrangements

The assignment will combine on-site work at our client Energinet in Erritsø or Ballerup with work from COWI’s offices or from home. The number of days you will work at the Energinet office will vary. You will work closely with project managers and other project participants, with the level of day-to-day presence at Energinet’s offices depending on the assignment. Travel to meetings, site inspections and other Energinet locations and projects may be required.

Location for the role is Kongens Lyngby.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• 
acting as a trusted operational partner to the Group General Counsel, helping manage priorities, communications, and leadership commitments

• 
preparing executive-level materials and reporting, including presentations, reports and performance metrics

driving legal operations and governance excellence by maintaining effective processes and supporting compliance with governance and regulatory requirements

• 
leading and coordinating strategic projects and legal transformation initiatives, including process improvements, AI and technology adoption, and implementation of new ways of working

• 
managing the cadence of the Group Legal Leadership Team, including agendas, meeting materials, minutes, action tracking, and escalation of critical issues

• 
supporting change management and organizational development initiatives by generating insights and recommendations that strengthen performance and decision-making

• 
serving as a key coordination point between Group Legal, COWI's Business Lines, and corporate functions, fostering stakeholder alignment and effective execution of strategic priorities

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future

Success in this role requires a collaborative mindset and a genuine passion for helping the team succeed together.

You are structured, proactive, and solutions-oriented, with the ability to navigate complexity and drive progress. You build trusted relationships across all levels of the organization, communicate with confidence, and continuously seek opportunities to enhance ways of working and create value.

In addition, you bring:

• a relevant master's degree, preferably in law, business law, or business administration, combined with 3 to 7 years of relevant post-graduate experience

Are you an experienced Senior Project Manager with a passion for electrical systems and complex infrastructure projects?

At COWI, we are strengthening our Project Management and Electrical disciplines within Renewable Energy. We are looking for an experienced Senior Electrical Project Manager who can lead multidisciplinary projects and help our clients develop resilient, sustainable and secure energy infrastructure.

You will work across renewable energy, power systems, electrical infrastructure, industrial facilities, transmission and distribution, hydrogen and PtX, energy storage, data centres and other critical infrastructure sectors. We do not expect you to be a specialist in all these areas, but you should bring a solid technical foundation within electrical engineering and experience from one or more of them.

Your profile. Together we shape the future

As Senior Electrical Project Manager, you will lead electrical and multidisciplinary projects from early advisory and feasibility studies through design, procurement and execution. Depending on your experience, you may also take a leading role on larger and more complex projects and support the development of our project management capability.

You will act as COWI's primary interface towards clients and key stakeholders while ensuring successful project delivery in accordance with COWI's project models, quality standards and values.

Your key responsibilities:

• Lead electrical and multidisciplinary infrastructure projects across various market sectors

• Manage project scope, schedule, budget, risks and quality throughout the project lifecycle

• Act as the primary point of contact for clients, partners, authorities and other stakeholders

• Coordinate multidisciplinary teams across electrical, civil, structural, environmental and permitting disciplines

• Support business development, tendering and proposal activities

• Drive collaboration across business lines and technical disciplines

• Support strategic client advisory and decision-making processes

• Ensure compliance with applicable standards, regulations and client requirements

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

You are a collaborative and commercially minded Senior Electrical Project Manager who combines a solid electrical engineering foundation with strong project execution capabilities. You thrive in technically complex environments, enjoy working closely with clients and specialists, and can take responsibility for increasingly large and complex multidisciplinary assignments.

We expect that you will bring:

• 
8+ years of relevant experience within electrical engineering, energy, industry or infrastructure, including solid experience in project management and multidisciplinary project delivery

• 
Strong stakeholder management and communication skills

• 
Experience leading multidisciplinary project teams

• 
A structured and proactive approach to project delivery

• 
A solid technical understanding of electrical power systems, electrical infrastructure or industrial facilities

• 
Ability to deliver projects safely, on time and within budget

A degree in Electrical Engineering, Energy Engineering or a related technical discipline is preferred, combined with a solid technical understanding of electrical systems and infrastructure. Relevant project management experience combined with a strong technical foundation may also be considered.
